title: Day 674 — Sheinbaum Rules Out Fracking Expansion in Key Basin, Citing Water Tables and Indigenous Communities
detail: On August 6, 2026 (Day 674, Thursday), President Sheinbaum announced that her government would not expand fracking (hydraulic fracturing) operations in a key northern petroleum basin, citing risks to regional water tables and nearby Indigenous communities. The announcement marked a partial reversal from an earlier, more open stance in which Sheinbaum had floated the possibility of 'new extraction technologies' distinct from traditional fracking methods as a way to boost domestic natural gas and oil output amid declining Pemex production. The decision underscored the balancing act facing her administration between reducing Mexico's growing dependence on U.S. natural gas imports and honoring environmental and social commitments central to the Fourth Transformation platform. The move followed years of pressure from environmental and Indigenous rights groups opposed to fracking expansion in northern Mexico.

media.caption: Sheinbaum announces her government will not expand fracking in a key basin, citing water and Indigenous-community risks

title: Day 674 — Sheinbaum's Approval Jumps to 57% as Inflation Cools to Near Six-Year Low
detail: On August 6, 2026 (Day 674, Thursday), Bloomberg News published new AtlasIntel LatAm Pulse polling showing President Sheinbaum's approval rating rising to 57%, an 8-point jump from the prior month's survey. The rebound followed a rocky summer stretch in which her approval had dipped below 50% for the first time in early July amid concerns over falling purchasing power and rising prices. Pollsters and analysts linked the improvement to two factors: annual headline inflation falling for four consecutive months — from 4.6% in March to 3.12% in July, the lowest level since May 2020 and back inside Banxico's target range — and Sheinbaum's increasingly vocal pushback against the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, including sharpened criticism of ICE following the July 7 killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston. The rebound reversed months of erosion in her approval that had been driven by the Q1 2026 GDP contraction, the CIA-Chihuahua sovereignty controversy, and broader economic anxiety.

media.caption: Sheinbaum's approval rating climbs to 57% as inflation cools to a near six-year low
